Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a coral-like N-doped carbon with in situ grown carbon nanotubes (CNC-CNT), derived from bimetallic core-shell MOFs, as an iodine host combining C–I chemical adsorption with physical confinement and extra electric double-layer capacitance. Significance: it enables 690 mAh g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹, 8000-cycle stability, and ~780 Wh kg⁻¹ pouch-cell energy density, offering a facile route to high-capacity, long-life aqueous zinc-iodine batteries.

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an electrolyte-first strategy using dual-site Al/F substitution of argyrodite sulfide electrolyte, guided by HSAB theory, to stabilize carbonyl cathodes and lithium metal simultaneously. 💡 The novelty lies in using iminodiacetic acid (IDA) as a multifunctional electrolyte additive whose tridentate coordination shifts zinc nucleation from progressive to instantaneous, yielding uniform deposition.
